clue.text: Something latched onto gold cake

indicators.note: placed on, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a gate is the thing most often fastened with a latch
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fastened item stuck onto a golden cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, the French word borrowed into English.

clue.text: Destruction of conifers, legal

indicators.note: destroying the trees breaks the word up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer's note that cutting down the pine trees was lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destruction of' tells you to rearrange CONIFERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic means relating to courts of law, as in forensic evidence used in legal proceedings.

clue.text: Charity event I snub, by and large disorganised

indicators.note: a disorganised set of letters has to be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they mostly avoid a charity event that is badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by and large' looks like an idiom meaning 'mostly', but its letters join I SNUB as fodder for 'disorganised'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bring-and-buy sale is a British fundraiser where people donate goods and buy others' donations, usually for a church or school.

clue.text: Arabian, possibly, consuming small pudding

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the Arabian is an example of a desert
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An Arabian horse, perhaps, eating a little pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabian' suggests a horse or a person; here it is the Arabian Desert, and 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the British word for the sweet course, synonymous with dessert.

clue.text: Musician showing popular rocking talent is about to play guitar

indicators.note: read loosely as 'next to', the following piece comes after

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer with popular talent is about to rock out on the guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' is loose here: the rearranged TALENT IS simply follows the guitar-playing piece rather than enclosing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a player of a musical instrument, one kind of musician.

clue.text: Nut securing top of uncoiled spring

indicators.note: holding something fast, so the other piece sits inside

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head, as is nut

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mechanical instruction: a nut holds the top of a spring that has come uncoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like hardware but is slang for the head; BONCE is British slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring and to bounce both mean to leap up energetically, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Festivals not starting, I'm afraid to say

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: galas are festive celebrations or occasions

explanation.surface: An organiser regretfully announces that the festivals are not going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' looks like news of cancellation but removes the first letter of GALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used where one might say 'I'm sorry to report'.

clue.text: Many miles off old Portuguese city

parts.note: something many miles off is far away

explanation.surface: A traveller remarks on a distant old city in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is the capital of the Algarve region in southern Portugal.

clue.text: Eggs in line, we hear

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: Someone reports eggs laid out in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish, eaten as caviar and the like.

clue.text: Pasta — much unfinished after ending in bin

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed after the single letter
takes the final letter of the word
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: oodles is informal for a great deal

explanation.surface: A cook throws most of the pasta into the bin at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' looks like a quantity of pasta, but it is the informal word for lots, with its tail removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a strip of pasta, so one noodle is a piece of that food.

clue.text: College official keeps me humble

indicators.note: holds within, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: a dean is a senior official at a college
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student complains that a college dean keeps putting them down.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to lower their dignity, a verb synonym of demean.

clue.text: Devil-worshipper transforms as saint beginning to tremble

indicators.note: changes form, so the letters are rearranged
takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Satan-follower turns into a saint who starts to shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforms' rearranges AS SAINT into SATANIS, then T begins 'tremble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Satan is one who worships the Devil, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A national lottery you can only lose once!

definitions.text: A national lottery you can only lose once!

parts.words: A national lottery you can only lose once!
parts.note: a game of chance named for a nation, where losing means death

explanation.surface: A wry quip about a gamble nobody loses twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is named after a nationality; the loser shoots themself, so nobody loses it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: In this deadly gamble a player spins a revolver holding one bullet and fires at their own head.

clue.text: Somewhat incompetent, all fingers and thumbs?

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy is described as all fingers and thumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all fingers and thumbs' is an idiom for clumsy, but taken literally it is a count of digits.
explanation.definitionFit: Two hands hold eight fingers and two thumbs, a count reaching that number.

clue.text: Rush scoundrel into trial

indicators.note: puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a court case is a trial
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A villain is hurried into the dock for his trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush of water pouring down is a cascade, also used as a verb for gushing.

clue.text: Turkish commander once more dropping in

indicators.note: losing, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: again means once more
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer is calling round again, dropping in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like visiting, but it removes IN from AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Sport that's restrictive?

definitions.meaning: the Olympic sport of swordplay with foil, epee or sabre
a barrier of posts and rails hems in an area, restricting it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which sport is all about limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the sword sport and the barriers that enclose a field.

clue.text: OK for one's teeth to cut into wire

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a cable is a thick wire
to hew is to cut with blows

explanation.surface: A dentist warns that biting into wire is not OK for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that can be chewed is safe and suitable to bite with one's teeth.

clue.text: Scent popular feeling on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the words sound like the result

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable; a sense is a feeling, as in a sense of dread

explanation.surface: A question whether the scent of public mood comes across in broadcasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is burnt for its fragrance, so it serves as a sweet smell.

clue.text: Surprisingly notable status in lieutenant ranked highly, though defeated?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the abbreviation
a surprising arrangement means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A notable lieutenant enjoyed high rank, though his side lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: coming at the end of a ranking is a defeat, yet the phrase says the last one counts highly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises the final one in a list as still important: high in esteem though at the bottom of the order.

clue.text: He painted a revolver, might you say?

definitions.meaning: An English painter of seascapes and light
something that turns, playfully, as one that revolves

explanation.surface: An artist is described as a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The great painter's surname also reads as 'one who turns', which a revolving thing does.

clue.text: Playground equipment to observe, now and then?

parts.note: to see is to observe, in the present tense for 'now'
then, in the past, observing becomes saw

explanation.surface: Someone watches the playground swings now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now and then' looks like 'occasionally', but it asks for the verb in present (SEE) then past (SAW).
explanation.definitionFit: A plank balanced on a central pivot that children ride up and down is a playground fixture.

clue.text: A pass between wingers in league game

indicators.note: the inner pieces sit between the outer letters
the wingers of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: taken as written
a cross is a pass across the field in football or hockey

explanation.surface: A footballer's pass travels between the wide players during a league match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Top primate, cross

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: The leading ape is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry', but it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something.

clue.text: Grey lair behind meadow

indicators.note: placed after, so this piece comes second

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A grey burrow lies behind the meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaden sky is dull grey like the metal lead.

clue.text: Cheese rind proper breakfast, say?

indicators.note: a rind is the outer layer, so the word's outside letters

parts.note: real means proper or genuine

explanation.surface: Asking whether cheese rind makes a real breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal is a typical breakfast food, so breakfast is given as an example of its use.

clue.text: Son is relative

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A statement that a son is a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Sis is short for sister, a relative.

clue.text: Spare prop

definitions.meaning: thin or meagre, as in a spare frame
to rest something against support, as a ladder against a wall

explanation.surface: A spare prop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both thin and to rest at an angle against a support.
